newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices extend losses on weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices extend losses on weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices continued to soften Tuesday as cooler-than-normal weather in parts of the South dampened demand, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were down nine cents to $2.16-2.20 per mmBtu, but these levels are still about 12 cents ahead of week-ago prices.
Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the low-$2.20s despite the ongoing maintenance on its Texas line.
The work will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Wednesday through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
Similarly in south Texas prices slipped several cents to $2.06-2.13.
Further east, where temperatures are also hovering below normal, New York city-gate prices slipped more than five cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Temperatures throughout the Northeast are expected to remain below normal through the week, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices also fell about five cents to $2.36-2.41 on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where much below-normal temperatures are keeping demand at a minimum, prices softened by about six cents to $1.95-2.00.
Detroit city-gate values were also weaker at $2.36-2.38.
In west Texas, Permian prices dropped another five cents to the low-to-mid $1.90s, while at Waha gas sold mostly at $1.97-1.99.
Trading was still fairly quiet at the southern California border due to the Santa Fe gas conference, but lingering heat in the Southwest pushed prices another two cents higher to about $2.17.
Meanwhile, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association's storage report have ranged from about 50 to 90 bcf, market sources said, versus a gain of 63 bcf a year ago.
